title: Postfix
description: Queue, delivery, inbound, TLS, postscreen and operations (postfix_exporter).

panels.title: Postfix
panels.description: Whether the queue can be read via showq. DOWN usually means: Postfix is not running.

panels.title: Log source
panels.description: Whether the exporter is reading the mail log or journal.

panels.title: Active / Incoming
panels.description: The fullest of the active, incoming and maildrop queues, as PostfixActiveQueueHigh checks them: per queue and server, not summed. Red from 500: that is where the alert fires (after 10 minutes). deferred and hold have tiles of their own.

panels.title: Deferred
panels.description: Messages whose delivery failed temporarily and will be retried. Red from 100: that is where PostfixDeferredQueueHigh fires (after 15 minutes).

panels.title: Hold
panels.description: Messages on hold (HOLD action, postsuper -h). They need manual intervention.

panels.title: Oldest deferred
panels.description: Age of the oldest message in the deferred queue.

panels.title: Delivery rate
panels.description: Share of successful delivery attempts (sent) in all attempts in the time range.

panels.title: Fatal / Panic
panels.description: Fatal errors of Postfix services in the time range.

panels.title: Accepted
panels.description: Messages accepted by smtpd in the time range.

panels.title: Delivered
panels.description: Recipients delivered successfully in the time range (all delivery services).

panels.title: Rejects
panels.description: Attempts rejected by smtpd restrictions in the time range.

panels.title: postscreen blocked
panels.description: Clients rejected by postscreen and failed tests.

panels.title: SASL failures
panels.description: Failed logins in the time range. Many of them point to password guessing. The alert PostfixSASLAuthenticationFailures fires from 50 in 10 minutes; the tile counts over the whole time range.

panels.title: Process failures
panels.description: Crashed or throttled Postfix processes (master).

panels.title: Unrecognised lines
panels.description: Postfix lines the exporter does not recognise. With --log.level=debug they are logged.

panels.title: Delivery attempts by status
panels.description: Attempts per recipient and minute, all delivery services.

panels.title: Delivery attempts by service
panels.description: smtp, lmtp, local, virtual, pipe ... as named in master.cf.

panels.title: Delay until delivery (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Time from arrival to successful delivery (delay=).

panels.title: Delay by stage (p95)
panels.description: delays=a/b/c/d: before the queue manager, in the queue manager, connection setup, transmission.

panels.title: Delivery attempts by DSN
panels.description: DSN codes in the time range: 4.x.x temporary, 5.x.x permanent (RFC 3463). More than 200 distinct codes appear as other.

panels.title: Reply classes
panels.description: Classified replies of the remote side (replies.delivery in the configuration).

panels.title: Bounce notifications
panels.description: Notifications generated by the bounce service (NDR, delay, DSN).

panels.title: Queue manager
panels.description: removed: message finished (delivered, bounced or expired). expired: returned to the sender after maximal_queue_lifetime; force-expired: via postsuper -e.

panels.title: Replies without status
panels.description: Replies of the remote side without a delivery status, e.g. greylisting on RCPT TO (replies.smtp in the configuration).

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Connections and regular disconnections with command statistics; the difference is aborted sessions. Values beyond the label limits appear as other (README: Bounded label values).

panels.title: Rejects by reason
panels.description: Classes from the reject text: dnsbl, relay_denied, unknown_recipient, client, helo, sender ...

panels.title: Reject texts in the time range
panels.description: Classified by replies.reject in the configuration.

panels.title: Aborted sessions
panels.description: lost connection, timeout and too many errors, by the last command.

panels.title: Failed SMTP commands
panels.description: From the command statistics at the end of a session, e.g. rcpt=0/1.

panels.title: SASL failures
panels.description: method other: a mechanism the client made up, often a scanner.

panels.title: Limits and reverse DNS
panels.description: Client limits enforced by anvil and broken reverse DNS entries.

panels.title: Logged-only rejects
panels.description: Rejects that warn_if_reject only logs. Shows, before a restriction is enforced, what it would reject.

panels.title: Access actions
panels.description: Actions from access tables other than reject: discard, hold, filter, redirect, warn, bcc.

panels.title: Outbound by trust level
panels.description: Anonymous/Untrusted: encrypted without a verified certificate; Trusted/Verified: verified.

panels.title: DNSBL score of listed clients (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Summed score from postscreen_dnsbl_sites for clients listed by at least one list. If p95 sits just below postscreen_dnsbl_threshold, the weights are worth a look.

panels.title: Milter actions
panels.description: Actions requested by milters (rspamd, opendkim, ...).

panels.title: header/body_checks and pickup
panels.description: cleanup processes every message, whether from smtpd or pickup.

panels.title: Process failures
panels.description: exit: process ended with an error; signal: crashed; throttling: master delays starting the service after repeated failures.

panels.title: Log lines of the exporter
panels.description: matched: turned into metrics; ignored: known, without a metric of its own; unmatched: unrecognised; foreign: other programs; invalid: not syslog format, or part of an overlong line.

panels.title: Message size (p95)
panels.description: Size of messages on entering the active queue.

panels.title: Last log line
panels.description: Age of the last Postfix line read. Red from 1 hour: that is where PostfixNoLogLines fires (after 10 minutes). On a quiet server this can be normal.

panels.title: Log source restarts
panels.description: How often the log or journalctl failed and was restarted in the time range.

panels.title: showq read
panels.description: Time taken to read the queue from showq. Red close to showq.timeout (default 10s): beyond it postfix_showq_up is 0, and with a large queue every scrape takes that long.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: 1 = one core.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: If it grows without end, the time series are growing: see the label limits in the README.
